passage:
Shalini watched Jeevan's name light up Eshaan's phone on the sofa arm and felt her stomach tighten. For days she had asked, in a light voice, "Who were you texting?" and "Why so long?" Her hand drifted toward the phone when he showered. She stopped herself. What she wanted was not the messages. It was the small cold feeling underneath.

Eshaan had noticed every one of the questions. He answered them at first, cheerfully, then with a tired patience. He felt watched in his own home and a little resentful, though he had done nothing but text an old friend. "I've told you, there's nothing," he said. "I'll say it once more, but I can't hand over my phone every night."

That Sunday Shalini set the tea down. "I'm not accusing you. I feel insecure when Jeevan's name comes up and I don't know why. Could you help me feel less alone with it?" Eshaan's shoulders dropped. "Yes," he said. "But if this keeps going, I want us to talk to someone together. I don't want to feel checked on."

Shalini nodded slowly, and did not reach for his phone.

qa.q: Whose name lit up Eshaan's phone on the sofa arm?
qa.a: Jeevan's name lit up the phone.

qa.q: How did Shalini's questions and Eshaan's replies look from each side, and what changed on Sunday?
qa.a: Shalini felt a cold insecurity and kept asking questions, while Eshaan felt watched and resentful even though he had done nothing. On Sunday she said plainly that she felt insecure, and he offered reassurance while naming a limit.

qa.q: What was Eshaan feeling as the questions kept coming?
qa.a: He felt watched and a little resentful, though he answered patiently at first.

qa.q: What could Shalini and Eshaan do if the insecurity comes back next month?
qa.a: Shalini can keep voicing the feeling instead of checking his phone, and they can talk to a counsellor together as Eshaan suggested.

grounding: A spouse's jealousy of a partner's friend is seen from the one feeling insecure and from the one who feels watched.
